rfp_text:
REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL — Cloud Migration

Section 2.3: All proposed servers must run a 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon Gold 6248R processor with exactly 384 GB of RAM. Section 6.1: Vendor shall carry general liability insurance of $10,000,000 per occurrence. Section 7.2: Cybersecurity monitoring tasks may be performed by qualified subcontractors with appropriate clearances.

risks.exact_quote: All proposed servers must run a 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon Gold 6248R processor
risks.issue_description: Brand-name and exact-model CPU specification eliminates valid equivalent hardware
risks.reasoning: Locking the spec to a specific Intel SKU prevents vendors from proposing equivalent or superior AMD/ARM/newer Intel processors. This typically violates federal procurement rules requiring 'or equal' language and inflates cost.
risks.impact_if_unresolved: Higher bid prices and reduced competition; potential procurement protest
risks.suggested_fix: Replace with performance-based specs (e.g., minimum core count, clock speed, benchmark score) and add 'or equal' clause

barriers.exact_quote: Vendor shall carry general liability insurance of $10,000,000 per occurrence

requirement_analysis.industry_standard: $1M - $2M per occurrence for similar IT engagements
requirement_analysis.justification_reasoning: Coverage level is wildly disproportionate to the contract scope and cybersecurity risk profile

barriers.impact: Small and mid-sized vendors typically cannot obtain or afford this coverage level
barriers.suggestion: Reduce to $2M per occurrence or scale coverage to contract value

questions.predicted_question: Will the agency accept equivalent processors that meet or exceed the listed specifications?

triggered_by.exact_quote: All proposed servers must run a 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon Gold 6248R processor

confusion_analysis.why_confusing: The RFP names a specific CPU model without an 'or equal' clause, which conflicts with standard federal procurement practice and is unclear about whether substitutions will disqualify a bid.
possible_interpretations: Strict requirement — only this exact CPU is acceptable
Performance baseline — any equivalent is acceptable
confusion_analysis.vendor_cannot_determine: Whether to bid the exact specified hardware (often more expensive) or a functionally equivalent alternative

questions.urgency_justification: Hardware choice drives both bid price and architecture; this must be settled before pricing
questions.impact_if_unresolved: Bids will diverge significantly in both architecture and cost
questions.suggested_fix: Add 'or equal' language and specify minimum performance requirements

opportunities.rfp_text: Cybersecurity monitoring tasks may be performed by qualified subcontractors with appropriate clearances
opportunities.reasoning: Cybersecurity monitoring is a discrete, separable scope explicitly invited for subcontracting and well-suited to specialized small businesses with cleared personnel.
